agree.reason: The nurse's-office evidence and the measured, non-overselling tone would win over many parents, but a board member who shares the athletic director's view or worries about cost gets suggestions rather than answers ("ask them how", a 7:30 supervised building with no cost attached), so a resisting reader may stay unconvinced.

honest.reason: The piece rightly refuses to promise a higher graduation rate, but it claims the other district "has been solving" the athletics problems with no support in the brief, rounds 72% up to a flat "three out of four" in the cost paragraph, and adds anecdotes like students arriving without breakfast.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that 412 visits beat the 369 from the next two periods combined, turns 640/890 into nearly three in four, and turns 84% into one in six not graduating on time, but it never puts the $180,000 into a per-student or per-day figure that would make it look smaller.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is set out fairly from the brief's numbers (short sleep, a crowded first-period office, an 84% graduation rate), but the brief gives no trend and the piece claims none, so the comparison is accurate but fixed at one point in time.

qualification.reason: Asking for yearly public tracking and a revisit "if the numbers don't move" names measurable outcomes, but it sets no target number, no review date and no specific consequence, so the reader can't actually check it.

objections.reason: All three objections are named honestly, but athletics is passed off to another district, the supervised 7:30 building quietly adds a cost of its own, and the $180,000 is weighed only through rhetoric.

fit.reason: This is a properly shaped op-ed with a headline, a clear ask before April 14 and a byline, and it runs about 650 words, right at the limit.
